items.item: Pre-commit and commit are deliberately separate steps: pre-commit must be safe to call before any crash, and commit must be safe to retry after one, which is exactly what lets recovery finish an interrupted write without risking a duplicate.

items.item: Idempotent-upsert and two-phase commit are two independent solutions to the same problem, not a fallback pair — a sink picks one approach, not both, since combining them adds complexity without adding safety.

items.item: The offset-atomicity requirement generalizes past Kafka: any system where 'how far we've consumed' and 'what we wrote' can be recorded separately has the same crash window, whatever the two storage locations are.

items.item: The three failure modes are independent on purpose: fixing one (say, making processing deterministic) does nothing to protect against either of the other two, so a production system has to address all three separately.

items.item: A transaction-timeout misconfiguration is uniquely dangerous among the three failure modes because it produces no error — the write simply never lands, and nothing in the pipeline signals that anything went wrong.

at.step: Prove it

items.item: Saying an idempotent-upsert sink reaches 'exactly-once' is really describing the effect of at-least-once delivery plus a write that happens to be safe to repeat — the delivery guarantee underneath is unchanged.

A deterministic id is the narrowest possible fix for duplication — it only works when the sink itself can recognize the overwrite, which is why the next topic generalizes the idea to any consumer, not just a sink.

at.step: Recap

items.item: Pre-commit's own durability doesn't require Flink's checkpoint barrier to have reached the sink yet — it only requires the sink's own staged write to be safely recoverable, which is a weaker, cheaper condition than full barrier alignment.

at.step: Reveal: durable first, visible only once confirmed

items.item: Both two-phase commit and idempotent upsert are stronger mechanisms than the delivery guarantee underneath them (at-least-once) — the exactly-once effect is built on top of at-least-once, not a replacement for it.
